clauses.current_legal_basis: Continuing under the original_plus_bounded_search route: the held original and the held later instrument (Executive Order 14085 section 1(a)); the held U.S. Code note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (release point 119-121, edition current through 2026-10-09) prints Executive Order 9158 as amended by Executive Order 9242-A and Executive Order 14085 and states no ending, and its first paragraph still reads in or with the named forces; the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog name no revocation or supersession, and the order has no own-terms end.

later_events.mechanism: amendment (strike and insert) of the first paragraph that Executive Order 9242-A restated: before, Army and Navy, any person, distinguishes or has distinguished himself, and the forces listed as Army, Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard; after, Armed Forces, those individuals, distinguish or have distinguished themselves, and Air Force and Space Force added to the forces listed; the words in or with, added by Executive Order 9242-A, are not struck

clauses.reason: The sole clause is the restatement of the first paragraph of Executive Order 9158 so that the Air Medal may be awarded for service in or with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard. No held instrument revoked or superseded it. Executive Order 14085 section 1(a) further amended the same paragraph by striking and inserting words but did not strike the words in or with that Executive Order 9242-A added; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, and the later amendment is recorded as a later event with the text before and after. The held U.S. Code note prints Executive Order 9158 as amended by Executive Order 9242-A with no ending statement on a release point current through 2026-10-09, so the clause was operative on 2026-10-14. Reviewer note: this is an amending clause whose wording is carried inside the parent order's text.

inventory_overrides.reason: The held text for 7 FR 7874 opens with the closing items 6 and 7 of the preceding order (Executive Order 9242), which the draft inventory took for this order's clauses. Executive Order 9242-A begins at the heading after them and consists of one operative paragraph, which restates the first paragraph of Executive Order 9158; characters 1535 to 2383 are that paragraph, from the words By virtue of through the closing quotation mark, and exclude the signature and filing lines.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text for 7 FR 7874 (PDF page 4 of the issue of 1942-10-06; text file EO_9242A of the fr-originals job) contains, at characters 1535 to 2383, the heading Executive Order 9242-A, Amending Executive Order No. 9158 of May 11, 1942, to provide that the Air Medal may be awarded to persons serving with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt at The White House on September 11, 1942 (F. R. Doc. 42-9873, filed October 3, 1942); the number, title and date agree with the register row. Inventory correction: that held text begins with the closing items of the preceding order (Executive Order 9242), so the draft inventory (items 6 and 7, characters 556 to 1143) describes a different order and is replaced by one clause, the operative text of Executive Order 9242-A, which has a single operative paragraph restating the first paragraph of Executive Order 9158. The restated paragraph differs from the original first paragraph of Executive Order 9158 by adding that the service may be in or with the named forces. Executive Order 14085 section 1(a) (signed October 3, 2022; 87 FR 60541) further amended that same first paragraph by striking and inserting words (Armed Forces, those individuals, Air Force and Space Force, distinguish themselves) and did not strike the words that Executive Order 9242-A added, so the amendment's wording is carried in the current text. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended; the later amendment is recorded as a later event with the text before and after. Reviewer note: the clause is an amending clause whose effect is carried inside the parent order's first paragraph, and Executive Order 14085 rewrote other words of that paragraph. Current law: the held U.S. Code note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (Office of the Law Revision Counsel release point 119-121, edition current through 2026-10-09) prints Executive Order 9158 as amended by Executive Order 9242-A and Executive Order 14085 and states no ending. Route original_plus_bounded_search: the held original, the held later instrument, no own-terms end, and the three bounded searches after reading their coverage notes. The U.S. Code search found one hit, the note above, and its edition ends 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected; the eCFR search (point in time as of 2026-10-14) found no hit; the Federal Register catalog notes held for the order are the Amends note under Executive Order 9242-A naming Executive Order 9158, a See note naming Transfer Order 30 of the Secretary of Defense dated December 10, 1948 (13 FR 8163), and the Amends note under Executive Order 14085; none is a revocation or supersession of Executive Order 9242-A. The order was unrevoked and its amendment remained in the operative text of Executive Order 9158 on 2026-10-14.
